subject: Private Offer / Marketplace unit-price calibration for BrightLayer
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Michael Carr <michael.carr@brightlayer.com>, Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@amazon.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-12T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up on private offer mapping & target $/1M tokens (BrightLayer)

Michael / Aisha — thanks again for the discovery earlier today. Quick recap and what we need to get to the marketplace private offer: 

Summary of BrightLayer ask:
- Production inference for analytics product (real-time enrichment + batch scoring).
- Target committed throughput: 450M inference tokens/month (peak bursts to 2k rps).
- Primary region: us-east-1.
- Goal: lock a private offer that maps marketplace unit price to an equivalent $ / 1M tokens for forecasting and chargeback.

Open items for pricing calibration / next steps:
1) AWS marketplace mapping: we need Aisha’s guidance on how a SaaS Private Offer SKU maps to a per-token unit for our quoting. Is the recommended approach a per-1000-inference-token unit or a per-vCPU-hour equivalent?
2) BrightLayer budget range & commitment: Michael, you mentioned a preferred annualized spend band — can you confirm $350k–$650k ARR or a monthly budget target?
3) Target unit economics: BrightLayer wants to target ~$120–$160 per 1M tokens initially (post-discount). We’ll test with quantized Llama-style models; Redwood will provide optimizations to reduce effective tokens (KV cache, partial prompt caching).
4) Required artifacts: procurement contact, PO window, and whether BrightLayer wants Marketplace Private Offer (AWS) or a direct vendor invoice.

Attachments: I’ll share a usage forecast spreadsheet and a redline-friendly draft of the PO terms (for internal review).

Request: Aisha — can you confirm the SKU mapping approach and whether AWS can issue a Private Offer that embeds an equivalent per-1M-token price (or point us to the recommended conversion methodology)? Michael — please confirm the budget band and procurement timeline so we can calibrate pricing.

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up on private offer mapping & target $/1M tokens (BrightLayer)

Sergio / Michael — great meeting. Short answers from AWS side: 

- Marketplace Private Offer model: AWS Private Offers are usually expressed as custom pricing for Marketplace listings (either usage-based or subscription). We can support usage-based pricing tied to a Marketplace product that bills per unit.
- Recommended unitization: for metering tokens, teams typically expose a custom usage dimension (e.g., "redwood_tokens") and meter per 1,000 tokens. That keeps invoicing simple. We can then convert requested $/1M tokens into $ per 1,000 tokens for the SKU.
- Conversion: $ / 1M tokens -> $ per 1k = (target $/1M) / 1000. So $150 / 1M => $0.15 per 1k tokens. Note that AWS marketplace and partner margins/fees may alter final vendor payout; we’ll model that.

What we need from BrightLayer: an expected monthly usage profile (hourly distribution if you have it) and any constraints on commit period (12 vs 36 months). If you’re open to a 12-month commit we can often secure a more predictable private offer price.

I’ll loop in the Marketplace billing specialist if you want us to draft the actual private offer SKU and price point.

— Aisha
Aisha Malik
Marketplace BD, AWS

Michael — thanks for the precise ramp and procurement contact. Attached is the quick mapping and a sample invoice simulation per your request. Short summary: 

Unit price conversions we propose (to be expressed as per-1k tokens in AWS SKU):
- Target band $110 / 1M => $0.11 per 1k tokens
- Target band $135 / 1M => $0.135 per 1k tokens
- Target band $160 / 1M => $0.16 per 1k tokens

Example invoice simulation (expected month = 450M tokens):
- At $0.135 / 1k => 450,000 (1k units) * $0.135 = $60,750 / month (~$729k annualized)
- At $0.11 / 1k => $49,500 / month (~$594k annualized)

Notes / assumptions:
- We are billing tokens as the sum of input + generated tokens after prompt normalization. If BrightLayer uses heavy on-device prefiltering or compresses prompts, token counts change materially.
- We’ll work with Redwood Optimize to identify 15–25% token reductions via prefix caching and quantization; those savings flow directly to spend.

Attachments: updated BL_usage_forecast_Q4Q5.xlsx (adds scenario columns) and redwood_po_terms_draft.pdf (clean copy).

Next steps: 
1) Aisha — if AWS can create a Marketplace Private Offer with a custom per-1k token metering dimension, please initiate the Marketplace SKU draft using $0.135 as the mid-band starting point.
2) BrightLayer procurement to review the draft PO terms and indicate legal turnaround time.
3) Redwood to share a short runbook documenting how metered events map to tokens to include in the offer.

Thanks — Sergio
